title: Med Spa Safety: How to Choose a Botox Provider
description: Med spa safety guide: who can inject Botox and fillers, spotting counterfeit products, questions to ask and what to do if something goes wrong.
h1: Med spa safety: choosing who injects your Botox and fillers
intro: Med spas are everywhere, and injectables are medical treatments. Here is how to choose a provider you can trust.

image.alt: Woman receiving a facial skincare treatment

cardText: Med spa safety guide: who can inject Botox and fillers, spotting counterfeit products, questions to ask and what to do if something goes wrong.

sections.html: Rules vary by state. Depending on where you live, injections may be given by physicians, physician assistants, nurse practitioners or registered nurses, usually under some level of physician supervision. Ask who your injector is, their license type, and who the supervising doctor is. You can check licenses with your state licensing boards.

The FDA and CDC have warned about counterfeit or unapproved botulinum toxin given by unlicensed people or in non-medical settings, with reports of serious harm. Ask to see the product box and confirm it is an FDA-approved brand obtained from a licensed source.

1. Who will inject me, and what is their training?
  2. Which product is being used, and is it FDA-approved?
  3. How are complications handled, and is there a doctor available?
  4. What is the total price, per unit or per syringe?

faqs.q: What are signs of a problem after Botox?
faqs.a: Seek urgent medical care for difficulty swallowing, breathing or speaking, drooping eyelids, blurred vision or muscle weakness after injection.
